title: Halt Fast! Early Stopping for Certified Robustness
claim: Adaptive early stopping matches full-budget certification accuracy with far fewer samples, and specialist variants recover accuracy where it matters.
layout: 3 line-plot panels in a row; shared x-axis; log-scale sample count on right
description: Three side-by-side line plots share a Certified Radius x-axis from 0 to 3.5. The left panel plots certified accuracy for Cohen 10k (solid black), Cohen 454 (dashed gray), KT Prior (red) and Optimized Meta-RS (blue). The curves fall from about 0.45 to 0, and the meta-learned curves sit just under the black baseline. The middle panel has the same black and gray baselines plus pink Small-R and cyan Large-R specialist curves. Each specialist tracks the baseline in its target radius range. The right panel plots sample count on a log y-axis from 100 to 10,000. Cohen 10k is a flat line at 10^4. The red and blue curves stay near 10^3, and the specialist curves swing widely across radii. Dotted horizontal lines mark the average counts. Colors are consistent across panels, and the legends sit inside each plot.
caption: Specialist Triage via Radius-Biased Stopping for CIFAR-10 at $\sigma=1.0$. (Left) Generalist accuracy parity with Cohen-10k using 22$\times$ fewer samples. (Middle) Specialist accuracy recovery in targeted zones ($R < 0.5$ or $R > 1.0$). (Right) Corresponding Sample Count ($N$) across radii, showing the significant compute reduction outside target zones. Metrics metrics represent the average for samples with a radius larger than $r$, following Equation [ref], except the dashed lines in (Right), which represent the average counts including rejected samples.
abstract: Randomized Smoothing (RS) provides rigorous robustness guarantees for neural networks without architectural constraints, yet its adoption is limited by extreme computational costs. Standard RS requires tens of thousands of model evaluations per input and forces practitioners to commit to fixed sample sizes a priori. In this work, we present a novel meta-learning framework for anytime-valid certified robustness that adaptively deploys computational resources. By using a lightweight meta-learner to predict image-specific priors for a sequential E-process, we achieve a 20-fold reduction in sample complexity compared to traditional methods while maintaining rigorous statistical guarantees. Beyond raw efficiency, we demonstrate how anytime-validity enables adaptively allocating compute based upon application-specific risk thresholds, a form of resource triage impossible under classic certification frameworks. That this is achievable while also providing similar certification performance demonstrates that our approach provides a pathway for real-time, safety-critical certification deployments.
